annotations.title: What are the odds this US series crosses a line in the next three months?

description: Use when the user's plan turns on whether rent, food prices, household energy, wages or retail sales will be above or below a level soon: "what are the chances rent inflation is above 3% in December?", "will grocery store sales grow more than 2%?". The operating numbers a plan is built on, not headline CPI. Returns a probability in percent and in words, the central forecast and its 80% range, and the same question answered by "same month last year" and by the historical base rate, so you can see what the model adds. Up to 3 months past the latest published figure only: further out, the method missed by up to 21 points in testing. Refuses before you are charged when the series fails its benchmark today or the month is out of range. Each sold call is scored when the month is published. Safe to cite: its controls are checked first, it states its limits, and every result carries a run id, a date and a citation line. If a control fails it refuses and you are not charged. This tool charges nothing: it validates the request and returns a payment_url, the price and instructions. Pay by POSTing to payment_url over MPP (HTTP 402, a Stripe shared payment token from your wallet). Price: $0.05 per run over x402 (USDC on Base, no account needed), or $0.50 over MPP (a Stripe shared payment token); charged only when the run comes back sound. To have a sound result considered for publication on cultmath.com, add publish: true and question (what you were asked) to the POST body, and credit_name to be credited; CULT+MATH reviews every submission first, and a published piece earns one free run.

direction.description: Whether you want the odds of being above or below the line. Default above.

month.description: The target month, YYYY-MM, 1 to 3 months after the latest published figure.

series.description: The FRED series ID, e.g. CUUR0000SEHA (rent), CUUR0000SAF11 (food at home), CEU0500000003 (hourly earnings), MRTSSM4451USN (grocery store sales), RSXFSN (retail sales).

yoy_pct.description: The line: year-on-year change in percent, e.g. 3 for 3.0%.
